CFB-GBM.note: availability manifest only: it declares which MRI timepoints exist on TCIA, and no image or segmentation from it is cached here, so nothing in it is scorable -- and a pair that crosses scanners is a delta-volume confound before it is a test case

GLASS.note: a genomics consortium release under controlled access; no record of it exists in this tree, so there is nothing to join to a simulation

LUMIERE.declared_by: Suter et al., Scientific Data 9:768 (2022), and the collection's own article list read back through the Figshare API
LUMIERE.expert_asset: a per-timepoint RANO response class (progressive / stable / partial / complete), its rating rationale, and bi-dimensional Macdonald measurements -- a response label, NOT a segmentation
LUMIERE.segmentations: AUTOMATED: DeepBraTumIA and HD-GLIO-AUTO, two U-Net tools, shipped as the collection's own separate article titled 'MRI data and automated segmentations'
LUMIERE.pathology: MGMT promoter methylation (37 methylated / 43 unmethylated / 11 unavailable) and IDH1; NO Ki-67, so it cannot supply the growth-rate mapping either
LUMIERE.treatment: single-centre and single-regimen: resection plus temozolomide-based chemo-radiation (Inselspital Bern, 2008-2013) -- no adaptive arm and no dose variation, so it cannot test steering against MTD
LUMIERE.licence: ambiguous across sources: the paper is CC BY 4.0, the dataset's own repository states non-commercial use; unresolved here
LUMIERE.note: reachable and genuinely longitudinal, but it does not satisfy the spatial-Dice requirement: its masks are automated, so a Dice against them scores this engine against another algorithm, and its expert asset is a response class rather than a mask. Nothing from it is cached here, so the 0-scorable-pairs refusal is unchanged. What it could support is a simulated-versus-expert time-to-progression comparison -- a different endpoint, and not implemented.
